newsitem.title: USA: Ohio post office is now Reindeer Station.
newsitem.headline: Ohio post office is now Reindeer Station.

text.p: The postmaster of this northwest Ohio town promised Thursday to hand-cancel Christmas mail with a special logo that includes a likeness of Rudolph, the red-nosed reindeer, and the words, "Reindeer Station."
With two full-time and two part-time workers, Rudolph's post office will have its inky hands full, given that last year's holiday volume nearly doubled to about 60,000 cards.
"We'll deal with it. We'll get all the cards out," postmaster Janis Butzier told Reuters. "It will be great."
Greetings from as far away as Hawaii and Italy have passed through Rudolph on their way elsewhere.

The town has been offering a special cancellation service at Christmas since 1991, capitalising on its nominal connection to "Rudolph, the Red-Nosed Reindeer," the popular Christmas song recorded in 1949 by cowboy movie star Gene Autry, which became the second biggest-selling single ever.

Stamped cards can be brought in person to Rudolph, about 20 miles (32 km) south of Toledo, or mailed in a large envelope or package (with its own correct postage, of course) to Postmaster, Rudolph, Ohio 43462-9998.
The town, population about 300, was originally named for local businessman Henry Rudolph in the 1890s, officials said.
